newsitem.title: MEXICO: Velazquez absent from Mexico May Day celebration.
newsitem.headline: Velazquez absent from Mexico May Day celebration.

text.p: For the first time in six decades, Mexico's top labor boss on Thursday was absent from the country's official May Day celebration, labor leaders said.
Fidel Velazquez, 97, who has rallied the powerful Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM) behind the government since the former dairy worker founded the CTM in 1936, stayed home due to poor health.

"Fidel is still sick and he won't be here," said Leonardo Rodriguez, secretary general of the national electricians' union and Velazquez's stand-in at the ceremony. "It's very significant that he won't because it's the first time he hasn't made it."

Velazquez has been a key figure in keeping a lid on labor unrest for the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI). He is also a key player in the government-business-labor alliance that sets country's economic goals and policy each year.
When Rodriguez took his place on the stage, he was lustily booed by the workers, who cheered when Rodriguez said his speech was nearly over.
President Ernesto Zedillo also celebrated with the CTM at the National Auditorium, and was to speak later Thursday.
Independent and radical left labor groups planned separate marches in the center of Mexico City.
